evidence: Top-level packages (app/domain, app/services, app/backtesting, app/infrastructure) broadly map to domain capabilities with clear naming: domain contains trading strategies and business logic, infrastructure handles external integrations, backtesting provides simulation capabilities
The centralized_config.py module is imported by 172 files indicating a god-module pattern that centralizes configuration but creates a single point of coupling

app/services/ contains 60+ subdirectories with mixed granularity: some are well-scoped (tax_efficiency, live_trading) while others appear to overlap in purpose (strategy_recommendation vs strategy_recommender, portfolio_construction vs portfolio_constructor)
The backtesting module shows good decomposition with clear subdirectories (services, engines, execution, validation) that map to backtesting workflow stages
Signal model is duplicated in both app/models/signal.py (52 importers) and app/domain/models/signal.py (42 importers) creating ownership ambiguity

The __init__.py files in key modules (app/services/__init__.py, app/backtesting/__init__.py, app/domain/strategies/__init__.py) provide clean public surfaces with explicit __all__ exports and STRATEGY_METADATA for self-documentation
README.md exists but is a tutorial-style document in Spanish that documents initial tasks rather than providing a high-level architectural overview of the current system
The engine hierarchy in app/engines/ (strategy_engines, portfolio_engine, risk_engine, etc.) provides clear domain-aligned decomposition for core trading operations
app/domain/strategies/ has grown to include many subdirectories (multi_factor, momentum_modular, learning) showing organic growth rather than planned decomposition

strengths: Clear top-level package separation: domain (business logic), infrastructure (external integrations), services (application services), backtesting (simulation) maps well to trading domain capabilities
Engine hierarchy in app/engines/ provides predictable change boundaries - each engine handles a specific trading concern (strategy execution, portfolio management, risk)
__init__.py files consistently use __all__ exports and module-level metadata (STRATEGY_METADATA) making public surfaces explicit and discoverable
Backtesting module shows mature decomposition with logical subdirectories (services, engines, execution, validation) that align with backtesting workflow phases
SOLID principles are documented and partially implemented, with service classes following Single Responsibility
high_level_elegance.issue_character: The primary issue is organic growth causing domain concept fragmentation and ownership ambiguity: multiple overlapping services (strategy_recommendation/recommender, portfolio_construction/constructor), duplicated models (signal.py in two locations), and a centralized_config.py module that has become a god-module hub with 172 importers creating tight coupling across the codebase.
high_level_elegance.score_rationale: Score of 72.5 reflects a codebase with solid foundational decomposition that has degraded through organic growth. The domain-aligned top-level structure and explicit public surfaces demonstrate intentional design, but the proliferation of overlapping services, duplicated models, and the 172-importer configuration hub indicate that change boundaries have become unpredictable. A new engineer would struggle to explain why both strategy_recommendation and strategy_recommender exist, or which signal.py to import from.

issues.summary: centralized_config.py imported by 172 files creates architectural coupling hub
evidence: Blind packet scan evidence shows centralized_config.py has 172 importers, making it the most imported file in the codebase
Module documentation claims Centralized Configuration System with REFACTORED STRUCTURE but the 825+ line file with nested imports creates a single point of coupling
Other god modules identified (backtesting/models.py: 102 importers, domain/models/market_data.py: 100 importers) follow similar patterns but centralized_config is the most severe
issues.suggestion: Consider decomposing centralized_config into smaller, domain-specific configuration modules (trading_config, risk_config, database_config) with a thin facade for backward compatibility, reducing the blast radius of configuration changes

issues.summary: Multiple overlapping service directories suggest unclear ownership boundaries
evidence: app/services/ contains both strategy_recommendation/ and strategy_recommender/ subdirectories - naming suggests similar purposes
Similarly, portfolio_construction/ and portfolio_constructor/ exist as separate directories
The services directory has 60+ subdirectories indicating organic growth without consolidation
issues.suggestion: Audit and consolidate overlapping services: merge strategy_recommendation into strategy_recommender (or vice versa based on actual usage), and consolidate portfolio_construction/portfolio_constructor. Document the ownership boundary for the surviving module.

issues.summary: Signal model exists in two locations creating ownership ambiguity
evidence: Blind packet shows app/models/signal.py has 52 importers
Blind packet shows app/domain/models/signal.py has 42 importers
Both files are listed as god modules with similar content descriptions (signal models, scoring, priority queue management)
issues.suggestion: Consolidate Signal model to a single canonical location (app/domain/models/signal.py following DDD conventions) and add deprecation warnings to app/models/signal.py with re-exports for backward compatibility

issues.summary: README.md documents initial tutorials rather than current architecture
evidence: README.md is a 670-line Spanish tutorial focused on T001 (FastAPI structure) and T002 (Configuration system) tasks
No high-level architectural overview, package organization diagram, or module responsibility documentation
A new engineer cannot use README to understand the current system structure or where to find specific functionality
issues.suggestion: Add an Architecture Overview section to README.md documenting: (1) top-level package responsibilities, (2) data flow between major components, (3) key extension points, and (4) links to domain-specific READMEs

issues.summary: app/domain/strategies/ shows organic proliferation without clear categorization
evidence: app/domain/strategies/__init__.py shows multi_factor import but README.md documents dividend strategy in app/strategies/dividend/ (different path)
Subdirectories include: multi_factor, momentum_modular, learning, config, and many individual strategy files
No clear strategy taxonomy or categorization scheme documented
issues.suggestion: Establish a strategy taxonomy (e.g., by asset class, by signal type, by time horizon) and reorganize strategies into categorized subdirectories. Create a strategies/README.md documenting the categorization scheme and where new strategies should be placed.

root_causes: Organic growth without periodic architectural review has led to service proliferation and model duplication
Configuration centralization was over-applied, creating a god-module instead of bounded configuration contexts
Missing architectural documentation (README, ADRs) means new code follows patterns of nearby code rather than intentional design
likely_symptoms: New developers asking which signal.py should I import from
Pull requests touching centralized_config.py causing widespread test failures
Inconsistent naming patterns (recommendation vs recommender, construction vs constructor)
possible_false_positives: The centralized_config pattern may be intentional for configuration consistency - requires confirmation from maintainers
Signal model duplication may be a deliberate staging area during migration - check for deprecation warnings or TODO comments
